fields.name: http_version
fields.description: HTTP version that is specified in the header.

fields.name: request_body_content
fields.description: Body of the HTTP request; usually specifies the exact content being requested.

fields.name: request_referrer
fields.description: The URL from which the request was referred, if applicable.

fields.name: requester_ip_address
fields.description: IP address from which the request was made.

fields.name: response_body_bytes
fields.description: Integer value corresponding to the total number of bytes in the response.

fields.name: response_body_content
fields.description: Content of the response (does not include header).

fields.name: response_status_code
fields.description: HTTP protocol status code in response header

fields.name: url_full
fields.description: URL to which the HTTP request was sent

fields.name: url_domain
fields.description: Domain portion of the URL.

fields.name: url_remainder
fields.description: the path after the root domain

fields.name: url_scheme
fields.description: type of user that initiated the request.

fields.name: user_agent_full
fields.description: User agent string associated with the request

fields.name: user_agent_name
fields.description: The user agent through which the request was made.
fields.example: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 7.0; SM-G930VC Build/NRD90M; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/58.0.3029.83 Mobile Safari/537.36

fields.name: user_agent_device
fields.description: Device type from which request was made, identified by user_agent substring

fields.name: user_agent_version
fields.description: User Agent Version. Note that some User Agent strings may not label versions in the same way.

objects.name: Email
objects.description: Email events are at the mail server level.

events.description: The event corresponding to an email being sent to an end recipient.
The event corresponding to an email being blocked by the email server.
The event corresponding to an email being redirected.
The event corresponding to an email being quarantined for security reasons.
The event corresponding to an email being deleted.

fields.name: action_reason
fields.description: The rationale given for blocking, redirecting, or quarantining an email.

fields.name: attachment_name
fields.description: Filename of any email attachment that may exist.

fields.name: attachment_size
fields.description: Filesize of the attachment.

fields.name: attachment_mime_type
fields.description: The MIME type of the attachment.

fields.name: dest_ip
fields.description: The destination IP address for the email.

fields.name: dest_port
fields.description: The destination port for the email.

fields.name: dest_address
fields.description: Recipient email address, taken from the SMTP "Recipient" field.

fields.name: date
fields.description: SMTP date header, which is actually a date time group.

fields.name: server_relay
fields.description: The Received portion of the SMTP header, which provides the chain of hosts that the email passed through during delivery; each link usually contains an IP address, domain, and datetime group.

fields.name: from
fields.description: Displayed sender name from the Message Information header; can be easily forged.

fields.name: smtp_uid
fields.description: Distint ID used to distinguish emails.

fields.name: message_links
fields.description: URLs extracted from the email body.

fields.name: src_address
fields.description: Email address of the sender, taken from the "Sender" SMTP field.

fields.name: src_domain
fields.description: The domain portion of the src_address.

fields.name: return_address
fields.description: Email address to which replies should be sent, also known as Return-Path or Reply-To; may differ from the src_address.

fields.name: message_body
fields.description: Content of the email, not including subject.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: Subject line of the email.

fields.name: src_ip
fields.description: Originating IP address.

fields.name: src_port
fields.description: Originating port.

fields.name: message_type
fields.description: Content protocol of the message body

fields.name: to
fields.description: the content of the To field in the email header; does not necessarily match up with real recipients.

reserved_ranges.purpose: sensor self-events (not CAR): service start/stop, configuration, provider enabled/silent, event drops, PPL availability — the 'going silent is a signal' hazard (brief §7)
